info.title: Forma Manager API
info.description:
The API of `forma-manager`, which deploys agents to multi-tenant Forma servers and keeps what they share: users' OAuth tokens (for MCP servers) and their conversations.

**The manager does not authenticate its callers.** It trusts `X-User-ID`, and anyone who can reach it can deploy, change and delete agents. It is meant to be called by your own back-end, on a private network, and must never be exposed to the internet. Your back-end authenticates the user, and sends their id.

Agents are sent as their *expanded* definition (`forma expand -f json`), which the manager compiles itself: with the deploying user's OAuth tokens, so that MCP servers can be reached. A multi-tenant runtime then serves each deployment to requests whose `X-Deployment-ID` names it.

post.summary: Checks an agent definition without deploying it.
post.description:
The definition is checked (ids, names), compiled (connecting to its MCP
servers with the tokens of `X-User-ID`, unless `mcp=unconnected`), and the
compiled agent checked as a runtime would before serving it. What it
reports is what the agent uses: what a deployment of it needs to be
granted, and what a user needs to be connected to.

parameters.name: mcp
parameters.description:
How the agent's MCP servers are treated: `connect` (the default) to
each with the caller's tokens, as running the agent would; or
`unconnected`, to check everything else without them, for a caller who
has not connected those servers yet. Without connecting, the names of
a server's tools are unknown, so whether they clash is not checked.

schema.description: How `/agents/check` treats the agent's MCP servers.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who checks the agent. Their OAuth tokens are used to reach its MCP servers.

requestBody.description: The agent's expanded definition (`forma expand -f json`): an [Agent](https://germolinal.github.io/forma/docs/reference_docs/auto-agent.html), with every `$file` inlined.

200.description: The agent compiled, and passed its checks

400.description: The definition is malformed, does not compile, or does not pass the checks; or `X-User-ID` is missing. The message says why.

422.description: The body is not an agent definition (an unknown field, a missing one, a wrong type)

post.summary: Writes an agent definition from a description.
post.description:
A language model (Gemini, on Vertex AI: the manager needs Google Cloud
credentials) writes the definition. Nothing is checked or deployed: check
it with `POST /agents/check` before deploying it.

500.description: The model could not be reached, or did not write a definition

put.description:
The new definition is compiled with the OAuth tokens of `X-User-ID`, who
must own the deployment, and replaces the old one: the runtimes serve it
from the next request on, in the same conversations. Credentials are
replaced only under the keys the request names.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who owns the deployment. Their OAuth tokens are used to reach its MCP servers.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or `deployment_id` is not a valid id

404.description: There is no such deployment, or it belongs to another user (which is not told apart, so as not to reveal it exists)

422.description: The body is not a redeployment

500.description: The agent did not compile, or could not be stored

post.description:
The definition is compiled with the OAuth tokens of `X-User-ID` (who owns
the deployment from now on), and stored. Multi-tenant runtimes serve it,
with no restart, to requests whose `X-Deployment-ID` is the id this
returns. Each call creates a new deployment, even for the same agent:
update one with `PUT /deployments`.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who deploys the agent, and owns the deployment. Their OAuth tokens are used to reach its MCP servers.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or the definition has no `id`

422.description: The body is not a deployment (an unknown field, a missing one, a wrong type)

500.description: The agent did not compile, or could not be stored. Check it first with `POST /agents/check`, which says why.

delete.description:
`X-User-ID` must own it. Runtimes stop serving it at once: requests that
name it are answered `404`. Its conversations are kept.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who owns the deployment.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or `deployment_id` is not a valid id

404.description: There is no such deployment, or it belongs to another user (which is not told apart, so as not to reveal it exists)

422.description: The body is not a deployment to delete

get.summary: Lists a user's conversations with an agent.
get.description:
The most recent first, without their messages. Conversations nobody wrote
in (every `/v1/init` starts one) are left out.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description:
The agent the conversations were held with: in a multi-tenant
runtime, the deployment's id; in a single-tenant one, the agent's
`id`.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: How many to list, at most.

200.description: The conversations, the most recent first

get.summary: Reads a conversation, with every message.
get.description:
What the runtime stored: the messages (user, assistant, tool), the calls
it waits on (`pending_tool_calls`), and what it keeps to resume them.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who owns the conversation.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or the id is not valid

404.description: There is no such conversation, or it belongs to another user

delete.summary: Deletes a conversation, with its messages.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who owns the conversation.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or the id is not valid

404.description: There is no such conversation, or it belongs to another user

patch.description: `GET /sessions` lists it under the new name (`display_name`).

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description: The user who owns the conversation.

400.description: `X-User-ID` is missing, or the id is not valid

404.description: There is no such conversation, or it belongs to another user

post.summary: Keeps the OAuth token a user obtained for an MCP server.

500.description: The token could not be stored

delete.summary: Forgets the token a user had for an MCP server.
delete.description:
Forgetting a token the user does not have is not an error. Agents
deployed already keep working until they are compiled again (redeployed):
a running agent reads the user's tokens when it is called.

500.description: The tokens could not be stored

AgentFeatures.description:
The capabilities a compiled agent draws on.

Recorded on a deployment so that everything downstream can act on it without
compiling the agent again: the front end badges an agent that talks to MCP
servers, and starring one that keeps a scrapbook gives the user somewhere to
read what it wrote.

asks_first.description: Whether the agent asks the user before calling some of its tools.

mcp_servers.description:
Every MCP server the agent talks to, in the order they are first
reached.

One server contributes a tool per capability it reports, and several
nodes may list the same one, so servers are deduplicated: what matters
downstream is which servers a user would have to be connected to, not
how many tools came from each.

models.description:
The language models the agent's steps run on, first-seen order: which
provider sees the conversation.

scrapbook.description:
Whether the agent keeps a scrapbook — the private store, one per user
per deployment, that outlives any single conversation.

tool_kinds.description:
The kinds of tool the agent uses (see [`agent::Tool::kind`]), each once, sorted:
what it can do, for whoever shows that in words.

workspaces.description:
Every workspace the agent's tools reach, and how — exactly what its
deployment has to be granted, and all it should be.

Derived from the tools, not from what anybody asks for: a knowledgebase
needs `read`, a workspace `read` and `write`. An agent can therefore have
less access than the person deploying it — a workspace they may edit,
reached by the agent only through a knowledgebase tool, is granted
read-only. Scrapbooks and code-execution runs are not listed: the
runtime derives them from whoever is calling, and grants nothing.

Sorted by path, scopes `read` before `write`, so the same agent always
reports the same list.

oneOf.description: Audio the model answered with.

content.description: What the model said: its text, and the files it produced.

name.description: Who wrote it, among several of the same role.

refusal.description: Why the model refused to answer, if it did.

thought_signature.description: The thought signature of the part.

tool_calls.description: The tool proposed made by the assistant

AudioFormat.description: Specifies the output audio format. Must be one of wav, mp3, flac, opus, or pcm16.

CachedToolResult.description:
Represents a cached result of a tool call,
to be used when resuming a session

Indicates whether the result is derived from a tool
in a root workflow, or not.

tool_call_id.description: Original ID of the tool call, used to identify the result

tool_name.description: The name of the tool that was called

ChatMessageState.description: State of a message, as reflected in the Database

CheckAgentResponse.description:
What `POST /agents/check` reports about an agent that compiled and passed
its checks.

features.description:
What the *compiled* agent turned out to use. Read from the finished
agent rather than its definition, so it covers tools reached through
nested workflows and servers that only name themselves on connection.

mcp_definitions.description:
The MCP servers the author configured authentication for, as written in
the definition — what a caller has to be connected to before the agent
can be compiled at all.

credentials.description:
What the deployment needs to reach what is outside it, by key; stored
encrypted (`FORMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). `whatsapp_api`
(`phone_number_id`, `access_token`, `verify_token`, `app_secret`) and
`telegram_api` (`bot_token`, `secret_token`) for the chat apps a
runtime serves it on, and `workspaces`: the workspaces its tools may
reach, as a list of `{"path": "<bucket>/<workspace id>", "scopes":
["read", "write"]}` (what `POST /agents/check` reports under
`features.workspaces`).

definition.description:
The agent's expanded definition (`forma expand -f json`): an
[Agent](https://germolinal.github.io/forma/docs/reference_docs/auto-agent.html),
with every `$file` inlined. It must have an `id`.

deployment_id.description:
The deployment's id: what requests to a multi-tenant runtime send as
`X-Deployment-ID`, and what conversations held with it have as their
`agent_id`.

allOf.description:
A file in a workspace, by reference. Never reaches a provider as it
is: resolving it puts the bytes in an `ImageUrl` or `File` part.

A file in a workspace, by reference. Never reaches a provider as it
is: resolving it puts the bytes in an `ImageUrl` or `File` part.

FormaMessagePart.description:
One piece of a message, as Forma keeps it.

The provider-facing parts are mirrored one to one, with the same serde tags
and field names as [`OpenAIMessagePart`], so every message stored before
this type existed reads back unchanged. What this adds is the parts that
only mean something inside Forma, and that have to be resolved into
provider-facing ones before a request goes out — see
[`TryFrom<FormaMessagePart>`](OpenAIMessagePart).

WorkspaceAccess.description: One workspace an agent reaches, and the access its tools need to it.

path.description:
The workspace, as a deployment's `workspaces` grant names it:
`<bucket>/<workspace id>`.

FormaTextPart.description: Represents a text part of a message.

text.description: The text content of the part.

FormaWorkspaceFilePart.description:
A file in a workspace, named rather than carried.

This is what an `attach` puts into a conversation: the bytes are fetched
and inlined only when a request is built, so a stored session stays small
(a 10 MiB PDF as base64 would not even fit one Mongo document) and the
conversation keeps working when the file behind it changes.

media_type.description: What the file was when it was attached, as the store reported it.

path.description: The file's path inside that workspace.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the file belongs to.

GenAgentRequest.description: What an agent should do, in words.

prompt.description: A description of the agent, as a person would write it.

oneOf.description:
Interactive OAuth 2.0 authorization_code + PKCE flow.

Call [`McpToolDefinition::authenticate`] once to complete the browser login
and obtain an [`OauthToken`]. Store that token and pass it to
[`McpToolDefinition::connect`] on every subsequent run.

Use this for MCP servers that act on behalf of a human user (e.g. Gmail,
Google Calendar, GitHub). The `client_id` must match a credential registered
with the authorization server and configured with `http://localhost` as an
allowed redirect URI.

Example:
```yaml
auth:
  type: oauth
  client_id: GMAIL_CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET   # omit for public clients
  scopes:
    - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly
```

callback_port.description:
The port to use for the OAuth 2.0 callback URL.
If not specified, a random port will be chosen.

client_id.description: Environment variable holding the OAuth 2.0 client ID.

client_secret.description:
Environment variable holding the client secret.
Omit for public clients that rely on dynamic registration.

scopes.description: Scopes to request. If omitted, the server's advertised scopes are used.

McpAuth.description:
Authentication configuration for an MCP server.

Credentials are read from environment variables at runtime and never appear
in config files or logs. Set the field to the name of the environment variable
that holds the value (e.g. `token: MY_MCP_TOKEN`).

McpToolDefinition.description:
Represents a tool definition for an MCP (Model-Client Protocol) server.

The server's tools are discovered at load time. `confirm_before_calling`
and `just_for` are applied to every tool; use the `tools` map to override
either value for specific tools by name.

oneOf.description:
Authentication configuration. Omit for unauthenticated servers.

The one strategy is `oauth`: OAuth 2.0 with a client registered with
the server's authorization server, on behalf of the user.

tools.description: Per-tool overrides keyed by tool name.

url.description: The URL of the MCP server.

McpToolOverride.description:
Per-tool overrides for an MCP server tool.

When present, these values take precedence over the definition-level
`confirm_before_calling` and `just_for` defaults. A missing field means
"inherit the parent value."

ModelSummary.description: One language model an agent runs on.

model.description: The model's name at that provider.

provider.description: The provider, as usage is reported under it (`openai`, `gcp.vertex_ai`…).

OauthToken.description:
An OAuth2 access/refresh token pair for a single MCP server.

Keyed by the server URL when stored in the tokens collection.
Call [`is_expired`][OauthToken::is_expired] before use; if true, call
[`refresh`][OauthToken::refresh] to obtain a new token.

access_token.description: The bearer token sent in `Authorization` headers.

client_id.description: The OAuth2 client ID used to obtain this token.

client_secret.description: The OAuth2 client secret used to refresh this token.

expires_at.description: The UTC timestamp after which this token must be refreshed.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token used to obtain a new access token when this one expires.

token_endpoint.description: The URL of the token endpoint used for refresh requests.

expires_at.description: When the audio stops being available to refer back to (Unix seconds).

OpenAICustomToolChoice.description: A call to a custom tool, as the model made it.

OpenAIFile.description: A file: a document, or audio in any container.

file_data.description: The base64 encoded file data, used when passing the file to the model as a string.

file_id.description: The ID of an uploaded file to use as input.

filename.description: The name of the file, used when passing the file to the model as a string.

OpenAIFunctionToolChoice.description: A call to a function tool, as the model made it.

arguments.description: The arguments, as a JSON string.

oneOf.description: How closely the model should look at it.

url.description:
A `data:` URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`), or a URL the model's
provider can reach.

format.description: The format of the encoded audio data. Currently supports "wav" and "mp3".

oneOf.description: Text.
An image.

oneOf.description: A recording, base64 with its format named.

allOf.description: A file, base64 in a `data:` URL.

oneOf.description: A file, base64 in a `data:` URL.

OpenAIMessagePart.description: One piece of a message's content, its `type` saying what it is.

oneOf.description: A call to a function tool: every tool Forma offers.

function.description: What is called, and with what.

id.description: The call's id, which its result (a `tool` message) repeats.

oneOf.description: A call to a custom tool.

function.description: What is called, and with what.

OpenAIToolChoice.description: A tool call the model made: its `type` says what kind of tool.

OpenAIVisionDetail.description: Tells the model what level of detail to use when processing and understanding the image

PendingToolCall.description: Represents a tool that is waiting for external feedback.

arguments.description: The arguments proposed by the AI

bundle.description: The bundle of the tool, for the same reason.

from_root.description: Indicates whether the tool call is from a root workflow, or not.

node_id.description: ID of the node that requested the tool call

tool_call_id.description: ID of the pending tool call

tool_name.description: The name of the tool to be called

tool_type.description:
What the tool is (see `SSEvent::ToolInputStart`), so a reopened
session renders the request as the live stream did.

RedeployAgentRequest.description: A new version of a deployed agent.

credentials.description:
Credentials to replace, by key; the deployment keeps every key not
named here. A new definition can need different workspace grants, so
the caller sends the `workspaces` it re-derived — and a channel's
secrets, which it does not resend, survive.

definition.description: The agent's new expanded definition, as in `POST /deployments`.

RemoveTokenRequest.description: Which of a user's tokens to forget.

mcp_url.description: The MCP server whose token is forgotten, as in `POST /tokens`.

user_id.description: The user the token belongs to.

RenameSessionRequest.description:
The body of a rename: what the conversation is called from now on. An
empty name — or a missing one — puts it back to the name derived from its
first message, which is what clearing the box in the UI sends.

name.description:
The conversation's new name, cut to 100 characters. Empty, or absent,
to go back to the name derived from its first message.

SaveTokenRequest.description: The token a user obtained for an MCP server, to keep.

mcp_url.description:
The MCP server the token is for: its URL, as the agent definition
names it (`url`). Agents look tokens up by it.

token.description:
The token. It is stored encrypted (`FORMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), and
refreshed when it expires.

user_id.description: The user the token belongs to.

SessionData.description: Data associated with a conversation, to be stored in the database

_id.description: The ID of the session itslf

agent_id.description: The id of the agent involved in this conversation

cached_messages.description: Contains the results of each node execution

channel_id.description: The id of the channel, as chosen by the developer (e.g., 'whatsapp' or 'web')

created_at.description: The date and time when the session was created

messages.description: The messages that have been exchanged in this session

name.description:
The name the user gave this conversation, if they renamed it. `None`
— which is every session that was never renamed, including all the
ones stored before this field existed — means the name shown for it is
derived from its first message by [`session_display_name`].

pending_tool_calls.description:
A flag indicating whether the session is suspended,
meaning that it is expecting external or human feedback.

running_since.description:
When the run now working on this session started, if one is. Set and
cleared through [`FormaDB::start_run`] and [`FormaDB::finish_run`],
which keep a second run from writing to the same history at once —
say, a user who left mid-run and came back to send another message.

tool_calls_results.description:
The result of the tools that have been called,
cached by the tool-call id

user_id.description:
The ID of the user who ownes this session. When a new
message is requested, Forma will check that the user owns
the corresponding session

variables.description:
Contains the variables available for templates of
runnables downstream.

SessionSummary.description:
A lightweight summary of a session, for listing a user's past
conversations without pulling in every message they contain.

display_name.description: A short label for the session, derived from its first user message.

ToolSummary.description: One tool an agent can call.

bundle.description:
The group it belongs to: the MCP server it came from, or the workspace
definition that expanded into it.

name.description: The name the model calls it by.

created_at.description: The time of creation of this

id.description: The ID of the message itslf

reactions.description: A collection of all the reactions

session_id.description: The session this message belongs to

user_id.description: The user that owns this message

FormaMessage.description:
A user, tool, assistant, or developer message, generic
over the potential DB id and date types

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: OAuth tokens a user obtained for MCP servers. Agents that use those servers are compiled, and run, with the tokens of the user they act for.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Agent definitions that are not deployed: checking and generating them.

tags.name: Deployments
tags.description: Agents deployed to the multi-tenant runtimes, which read them from the database. A deployment's id is what requests to a runtime send as `X-Deployment-ID`.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Users' conversations, as the runtimes stored them. In a multi-tenant runtime, a conversation's `agent_id` is the id of the deployment it was held with.
